'''Alasdair Ian Fenton Urquhart''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|l|ə|s|d|ər|_|ˈ|ɜr|k|ər|t}} {{respell|AL|ist|ər|_|UR|kərt}}; born 20 December 1945) is a Scottish–Canadian philosopher and [[emeritus]] professor of [[philosophy]] at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Alasdair Urquhart |url=https://philosophy.utoronto.ca/directory/alasdair-urquhart/ |access-date=2022-08-22 |website=Department of Philosophy |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=April 1998 |title=Alasdair Urquhart's Curriculum Vita |url=https://stanford.library.sydney.edu.au/archives/fall2003/subject-editors/urquhart.html |access-date=2022-08-22 |website=stanford.library.sydney.edu.au}}</ref> He has made contributions to the field of [[logic]], especially [[non-classical logic]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-71430-7 |title=Alasdair Urquhart on Nonclassical and Algebraic Logic and Complexity of Proofs |series=Outstanding Contributions to Logic |year=2022 |volume=22 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-71430-7|isbn=978-3-030-71429-1 |editor1=Düntsch, Ivo |editor2=Mares, Edwin }}</ref> Amongst his most notable accomplishments is the proof of [[decidability (logic)|undecidability]] of the [[relevance logic]] '''R'''. He published numerous scientific papers in [[theoretical computer science]] venues, mostly on [[mathematical logic]] topics of [[logic in computer science|relevance to computer science]].

== Early life ==
Urquhart is a native of Scotland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.whockey.com/work/dcs/dcs/people/faculty/urquhart.html|title=Alasdair Urquhart was born in Scotland in 1945|publisher=Department of Computer Science – University of Toronto|accessdate=2 April 2010}}</ref> He received his [[MA (Scotland)|MA]] in philosophy from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1967.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He then attended the [[University of Pittsburgh]], receiving an MA and Ph.D. in 1973 under the supervision of [[Alan Ross Anderson]] and [[Nuel Belnap]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />  

== Career ==
From 1973 to 1975, Urquhart was an assistant professor at the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]] (then known as Erindale College).<ref name=":1" /> He became an associate professor there in 1975.<ref name=":1" /> Starting in 1986, Urquhart was a professor of [[philosophy]] in the [[University of Toronto Faculty of Arts and Science]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> 

From 1983 to 1989, Urquhart was a consulting editor for the ''[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]''.<ref name=":1" /> He was also an editor of ''Canadian Philosophical Monographs''.<ref name=":1" /> In 2003, he became the managing editor of reviews for ''[[The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic]]''.<ref>Leng, Mary. "Reviews". ''The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic'' 8, no. 4 (2002): 516. {{doi|10.2307/797954}}. </ref> 

He is currently on the Council of the Division for Logic, Methodology and Philosophy of Science and Technology of the [[International Union of History and Philosophy of Science|International Union of History and Philosophy of Science and Technology]] (2020–2023).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dlmps.org/pages/council/council-2020-2023.php|title=DLMPST Website: Council 2020-2023|accessdate=16 April 2020}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* Urquhart, Alasdair and [[Nicholas Rescher|Rescher, Nicholas.]] ''Temporal Logic.'' New York'':'' Springer Verlag, 1971. {{ISBN|978-3-7091-7664-1}}
* Urquhart, Alasdair. "The Undecidability of Entailment and Relevant Implication."  ''[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]'' 49:4 (1984): 1059–1073.<ref name=":0" />
* Urquhart, Alasdair and [[Stephen A. Cook|Cook, Stephen A.]] "Functional Interpretations of Feasibly Constructive Arithmetic", ''[[Annals of Pure and Applied Logic]]'', 1993; preliminary version at [[Symposium on Theory of Computing|STOC]]'89
* "The Complexity of Decision Procedures in Relevance Logic II", ''Journal of Symbolic Logic'' 64:4 (1999): 1774–1802.
